Where is Denver and how big is the housing market?

Denver is the capital of Colorado and its largest city, sitting in the South Platte River valley just east of the Front Range. The Census Bureau counted 715,522 residents in 2020 and estimated 740,613 for July 1, 2025.

The city is also a county. Denver became a consolidated city and county in 1902, so one government handles both municipal services and the county duties of assessing, taxing and recording property. For a seller, that means fewer offices to deal with than in most Colorado towns.

All of these come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for 2020 to 2024. Fewer than half of Denver homes are owner-occupied, so a good share of sellers here are landlords, heirs or people who bought a rental and want out.

How did Denver grow into the city it is today?

Denver was platted in 1858 where Cherry Creek meets the South Platte River, during the Pikes Peak gold rush. It was named for Kansas Territorial Governor James W. Denver, incorporated as Denver City in 1861 and shortened to Denver in 1866.

It became the territorial capital in 1867, and an 1881 referendum made it the permanent state capital.

Elevation is officially 5,280 feet, the source of the Mile High nickname. The city covers roughly 153 square miles of land and is divided into 78 official neighborhoods used for planning, including LoDo, RiNo, Park Hill, Uptown, the Golden Triangle and Central Park, which was formerly Stapleton.

Who employs people in Denver?

Government, health care, education and aviation lead the list of Denver's largest employers. The city's own 2023 financial report names these five at the top:

  • City and County of Denver: 13,584 employees
  • Denver Public Schools: 12,693
  • State of Colorado: 10,686
  • Denver Health and Hospital Authority: 9,502
  • United Airlines: 7,230

The Denver metro area's gross metropolitan product was $311.9 billion in 2023, and eight Fortune 500 companies have headquarters in the city. Census data shows 74.2% of Denver residents aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the mean commute is 24.9 minutes.

Steady public-sector and hospital jobs keep demand for housing close to downtown, but they do not protect an individual owner from a job loss, a divorce or an inherited house that nobody wants to manage.

What does Denver weather mean for a house?

Hail is the weather risk that matters most for Denver roofs. Denver ranks 10th among U.S. cities with at least 50,000 people for hail proneness and has had three of the ten costliest hailstorms in the country.

The climate is cool and semi-arid, with about 3,100 hours of sunshine a year and average snowfall of 53.5 inches. July highs average 89.9 degrees, and the record high is 105 degrees, set June 28, 2018.

A hail-damaged roof, cracked siding or an unrepaired insurance claim can slow a traditional sale, because buyers' lenders and inspectors look hard at roofs. Sellers in Denver often face these questions:

  • Was the hail damage ever claimed and repaired, or just left?
  • How old is the roof, and will a buyer's insurer cover it?
  • Do sun and freeze-thaw cycles show up in the stucco, deck or exterior paint?

How do property taxes work when you sell a Denver house?

Denver taxes are billed after the year they cover, and the city's Treasury Division collects them. The Treasury page lists two ways to pay: two installments, due the last day of February and June 15, or a single payment due April 30. If a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

Statements are now online. An owner searches the address in Denver's property search tool, opens the Tax Documents section and downloads the statement for the year. Paying by credit or debit card carries a 2.5% service fee, while an electronic check avoids it. Treasury's phone number is 720-913-9300.

At a closing, the title company usually prorates the current year's taxes between seller and buyer. Treasury also offers a Certificate of Taxes Due for Real Property, a document title companies use to confirm what is owed on a parcel. Unpaid prior years must be cleared before a clean transfer.

For appeal rights and assessment timing, see the Denver Treasury property tax page.

What is the state fee when a Denver deed is recorded?

Colorado charges a documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 on transfer deeds where the consideration is more than $500. County recording pages describe it that way, and on a $500,000 sale it works out to $50.

Denver records deeds in the same county system, so the fee, the recording charge and any transfer paperwork appear on the settlement statement. A cash sale does not change these steps, but it can shorten the time between signing and recording because no lender has to fund the loan first.

What rental and short-term rental rules affect Denver sellers?

Denver requires a license for every short-term rental, and the rental must be the host's primary residence. Hosts also have to show their business license number in every advertisement, and those who break the rules can be fined or lose the license.

That rule matters if you own a second Denver property that was operating as an Airbnb. A primary-residence requirement means a non-owner-occupied house cannot lawfully run as a short-term rental, so the house may have to be sold or converted to a long-term rental. The same house can be worth less to a buyer who counted on nightly rental income.

The city's rental, zoning and licensing pages are the place to confirm what applies to your address before you list or accept an offer.

What are the ways to sell a Denver house?

Most Denver owners choose among three routes: list with an agent, sell on their own, or accept a cash purchase. Each route trades price against time and effort.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the highest sale price on a house in good condition, but with showings, repairs requested after inspection and a buyer's loan approval to wait for.
  • Selling on your own: saves the agent's commission but leaves pricing, disclosures and paperwork to you.
  • Cash sale: a buyer purchases the house as it stands, so there is no repair list and a closing date you can often choose.

A cash route fits a house with deferred maintenance, a hail-damaged roof, a tenant in place or an estate that needs to settle. A listing usually fits a clean house with time on the calendar. You can compare both before deciding, and a cash offer from us carries no obligation.

More questions about Denver, CO

How much is the median home worth in Denver?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figure for the median value of owner-occupied homes in Denver is $616,000. Individual houses vary a great deal with condition, neighborhood and lot size, so treat it as a citywide benchmark and not a price for your house.

When are Denver property taxes due?

Denver's Treasury page lists the last day of February and June 15 for two installments, or April 30 for one full payment. A due date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

Can I sell a Denver house that was used as a short-term rental?

Yes. Denver's rules require a license and a primary-residence host, so a house that lacked either may have compliance issues a buyer will ask about. A cash buyer can purchase it as it stands, though you should settle any city fines or unpaid taxes.

Does hail damage stop me from selling a house in Denver?

No. Denver is among the most hail-prone large cities, so buyers expect to see it. A damaged roof can lower the price or complicate a buyer's financing, which is why many owners with roof damage consider an as-is cash sale.

What is the state documentary fee in Colorado?

It is $0.01 per $100 of consideration on a deed over $500, as county recording pages describe it. On a $500,000 sale that is $50.

Where is Colorado Springs and how large is it?

Colorado Springs is the county seat of El Paso County, about 70 miles south of Denver on Fountain Creek, near the base of Pikes Peak. It covers 195.761 square miles, the largest area of any Colorado municipality.

The Census Bureau counted 478,961 residents in 2020, up from 416,427 in 2010, and estimated 494,743 for July 1, 2025. That makes it the second most populous city in the state. The city sits at about 6,011 feet, which is roughly 700 feet higher than Denver.

The figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table and Wikipedia's city entry. A large owner-occupied share means many Colorado Springs sellers are homeowners moving on a deadline, often tied to a military assignment or a job change.

What is the history of Colorado Springs in brief?

The area began with Colorado City, organized August 13, 1859, during the Pikes Peak gold rush. Fountain Colony was renamed Colorado Springs in 1871, the county seat moved over in 1873, and the town was incorporated on June 19, 1886.

The military arrived later and shaped the modern city. Camp Carson, now Fort Carson, was established in 1941. In 1950 Ent Air Force Base was chosen as the Air Defense Command headquarters, and Peterson Field reopened as an Air Force base in 1951. Most of the former Ent base became a U.S. Olympic training center in 1977.

The city's government changed in 2010, when it adopted a council and strong mayor system. The nine-member council has six district seats and three at-large members.

Which employers drive the Colorado Springs economy?

The military, high-tech industry and tourism lead the local economy, in that order. Wikipedia reports about 45,000 active-duty troops in the area as of 2021, plus more than 100,000 veterans, and says the military and defense contractors supply more than 40% of the Pikes Peak region's economy.

  • Installations: Fort Carson, the U.S. Air Force Academy, Peterson Space Force Base, Schriever Space Force Base and Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station.
  • Defense contractors named include Northrop Grumman, Boeing, General Dynamics, L3Harris and Lockheed Martin.
  • Tourism supplies more than 16,000 jobs in the region.

Unemployment was 4.6% in April 2025. Military and defense employment is a large part of the local economy, so buyer demand can shift with major employer decisions.

What does the Colorado Springs climate and wildfire history mean for a house?

Colorado Springs has a semi-arid climate with about 243 sunny days a year, around 16.5 inches of precipitation and 38 inches of snow in an average season. March is the snowiest month, and most of the rain arrives in July and August with the monsoon.

The city averages 18 days a year at or above 90 degrees and 5.2 nights below zero. It is also among the most active lightning-strike areas in the country. Those swings in temperature stress roofs, gutters, decks and exterior paint.

Wildfire is part of the city's recent memory. The Waldo Canyon fire began June 23, 2012, about 4 miles northwest of the city, destroyed 347 homes within the city and forced 32,000 residents to evacuate. The Black Forest fire the next year was more destructive. Owners should ask their insurer how wildfire risk is treated for their address.

How do property taxes and tax dates work for Colorado Springs sellers?

El Paso County bills and collects taxes on Colorado Springs property. The county Treasurer's Important Dates page lists these steps in the cycle:

  • January 10: the Assessor certifies the tax warrant to the Treasurer.
  • January 28: statements must be mailed.
  • Last day of February: the first half is due.
  • April 30: the full-year payment option is due.
  • June 15: the second half is due, and unpaid taxes become delinquent afterward.

Delinquent real estate taxes are advertised in September and sold at public auction in October. After September 30 the Treasurer requires cash or certified funds. A deadline on a weekend or legal holiday carries to the next business day.

At closing the title company calculates what the seller owes through the closing date. Any tax lien from a prior year must be redeemed first, and redemption payments must reach the Treasurer by the last business day of the month. Read the El Paso County Treasurer's dates page for the current year.

What are the short-term rental rules in Colorado Springs?

Colorado Springs requires a permit for any rental of 29 days or less. The permit costs $124.95, lasts one year and must be renewed without a lapse, because the city says there is no grace period.

Applicants must show proof of primary residence, at least $500,000 in liability insurance and a link to their hosting platform listing. Two separate units on one property need two separate permits. City staff has 10 business days to review a complete application. For a non-owner-occupied rental, a lapsed permit can mean forfeiture of the established permit, which affects what a buyer will pay for a house sold as a rental business.

How do roads, neighborhoods and the airport shape Colorado Springs?

Interstate 25 runs through the city for nearly 18 miles, and Powers Boulevard (State Highway 21) is a major semi-expressway on the east side. Other routes include Highways 83, 94 and 115, U.S. 24 and U.S. 85.

Colorado Springs Airport, open since 1925, is the second-largest commercial airport in Colorado and handled 2,134,618 passengers in 2022. Named areas include Old Colorado City, Broadmoor, Ivywild, Knob Hill, Roswell, the Old North End and Banning Lewis Ranch. Mean travel time to work was 22.7 minutes in 2020 to 2024 Census data, and sellers can point to that when describing a house near the interstate or Powers.

How can you sell a Colorado Springs house quickly?

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself or accept a cash purchase, and the right choice depends on condition and timing. Military families with orders, heirs settling an estate and landlords with a vacant rental often put speed first.

  • A listing can bring a higher price for a house in good shape, with showings and buyer financing to wait for.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale saves the agent's fee but puts disclosures and paperwork on you.
  • A cash purchase is as-is, so repairs, wear and a hail or fire-season insurance question do not hold up closing.

We buy houses in Colorado Springs and nearby parts of El Paso County in any condition. Tell us about the property and we will review it, with no obligation if you decline.

What is the median home value in Colorado Springs?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figure for the median value of owner-occupied homes in Colorado Springs is $452,600. That is a citywide benchmark. Your own house depends on condition, location and lot.

When are El Paso County property taxes due?

The first half is due the last day of February, the full-year option on or before April 30 and the second half June 15. The Treasurer's page says unpaid taxes become delinquent after the second half deadline.

Do I need a permit to rent my Colorado Springs house on Airbnb?

Yes, for stays of 29 days or less. The city's permit is $124.95, lasts one year and requires proof of primary residence and $500,000 in liability insurance.

Does wildfire risk affect selling a house in Colorado Springs?

It can. The 2012 Waldo Canyon fire destroyed 347 homes in the city, so buyers and insurers in wooded areas ask about fire risk. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands.

Can I sell a Colorado Springs house while on military orders?

Yes, and a cash sale avoids waiting on a buyer's loan, which helps when an assignment date is fixed. Ask the title company early what signing arrangements it accepts if you are away.

How big is Aurora and where does it sit?

Aurora is a home rule city in Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, and it is a principal city of the Denver metro area. It covers about 163.6 square miles, which makes it second in Colorado by land area and roughly 6% larger than Denver.

The 2020 census counted 386,261 residents (336,035 in Arapahoe County, 47,720 in Adams County and 2,506 in Douglas County). The 2025 estimate of 410,053 makes Aurora the third largest city in the state. Because the city touches three counties, your county depends on the address.

Elevation runs from about 5,285 feet near Sand Creek to 6,229 feet at the southern border, nearly a thousand feet of difference across one city.

How did Aurora get its name?

The area was platted around 1890 or 1891 as Fletcher, after Denver businessman Donald Fletcher, and incorporated as the Town of Fletcher on May 5, 1903. It was renamed Aurora in 1907 after one of its subdivisions.

It reincorporated as a city on March 9, 1928, and became one of the fastest growing cities in the country in the late 1970s and early 1980s. That growth explains why so much of its housing is from the 1970s and later.

The Anschutz Medical Campus includes the former Fitzsimons Army Hospital site and the Fitzsimons Life Science District, and Buckley is described as the city's largest employer. A house close to any of these sites sits in a different setting from one near the southern edge of the city.

What areas and school districts make up Aurora?

Aurora is a patchwork of districts. Aurora Public Schools (Adams-Arapahoe 28J) is the main one, and Cherry Creek Public Schools, Bennett 29-J, School District 27J and Douglas County RE-1 serve other parts.

  • Lowry Campus, the former Lowry Air Force Base
  • Downtown A-Town, the historic Fletcher townsite
  • Aurora Highlands, Heather Gardens, Meadowood and Mission Viejo

Part of Stapleton is also inside Aurora. The district on your tax bill and your buyer's school search both depend on the exact address.

What should an Aurora seller know about Arapahoe County?

Most of Aurora sits in Arapahoe County, which was founded November 1, 1861, covers 805 square miles and had 655,070 residents in 2020, making it the third most populous county in Colorado. Littleton is the county seat, and Aurora is the largest city.

The county stretches 72 miles east to west but only 4 to 12 miles north to south, and it is 97.9% urban. Other cities in it include Centennial, Englewood, Greenwood Village and Cherry Hills Village, so a buyer comparing homes may be weighing several neighboring tax districts at once.

Adams and Douglas county addresses follow their own offices, and your bill and closing paperwork come from the one that matches your parcel.

How do roads, rail and weather shape life in Aurora?

I-70, I-225 and the E-470 beltway cross the city. RTD's H Line serves Dayton and Nine Mile stations, and the R Line reaches Peoria Station, where riders transfer to the A Line to Denver Union Station and Denver International Airport.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 18.2 inches of precipitation a year. July highs average 89 degrees and December lows average 17. Tornado warnings are common between April and July, though the tornadoes are usually weak, and the first snow usually arrives in late October. Roofs and windows are the items a buyer's inspector will check first.

Is Aurora adding rental rules?

Aurora has long run an apartment inspection program, and the city council has been weighing a rental registration and licensing program that would cover multifamily and single family rentals. Staff described the idea as yearly registration with a local contact for each rental.

The Sentinel reported that the idea was raised at a June study session, that any program would need council approval first, and that staff would study the cost and fees. If you own a rental here, check the city's current rules before you list, because registration status can affect a sale.

How does property tax work in Aurora?

Aurora spans three counties, so the bill comes from Arapahoe, Adams or Douglas County, depending on where the house is. The Arapahoe County Treasurer collects tax on the largest share and can be reached at 303-795-4550.

  • 2025 was a revaluation year, and Arapahoe noted that a temporary state exemption used in 2023 and 2024 had expired.
  • Arapahoe lists a senior and military deferral, with applications from January 1 through April 1.
  • The Treasurer takes requests for a Certificate of Taxes Due, used at closing.
  • Residential rates for 2026 are listed as 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.

What does the Arapahoe County Treasurer offer sellers?

The Treasurer's page lists several tools that matter in a sale: Certificate of Taxes Due requests for individuals and title companies, an address change request for your tax mailing address, delinquent tax publications and tax lien sale information. It also covers a manufactured home buying and selling process.

Excess foreclosure funds are now handled by the Public Trustee rather than the Treasurer. Owners can opt out of paper statements through the Go Paperless form, and email alerts are available when a statement is posted online.

  • Phone: 303-795-4550 for the Treasurer's office.
  • Tax Search page: view or pay taxes, statements and receipts.
  • Deferral: for seniors and military, January 1 through April 1.

Older owners who plan to sell should ask whether any deferred tax has to be repaid at closing.

What is the Aurora population mix and density?

Aurora's density is about 2,412 people per square mile, and about 30% of residents are Hispanic or Latino, according to the 2020 census figures on Wikipedia. The city is large and spread out, and its neighborhoods range from a historic downtown to the Lowry and Anschutz campuses.

Aurora ranks 54th among US cities by land area, and the city grew from a small town named Fletcher into the 50th largest city in the nation. For a seller, that size means comparable sales a few miles apart can differ, and a local review of your own block is more useful than a citywide figure.

How can you sell a house in Aurora?

You can list it, sell by owner, or take a cash offer. Cash works well when the house needs repairs, has tenants, or sits in a probate or relocation timeline.

We buy as is. Send your Aurora address and we will tell you how a sale would work, including the tax figures that title will ask for.

It depends on the address. Aurora lies in Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, and most residents are in Arapahoe County.

Does Aurora have a rental license?

The city council has been considering a registration and licensing program for rentals, which would require council approval. Check the city for the current status.

Littleton is the county seat of Arapahoe County, though Aurora is the most populous city in it.

What kind of city is Fort Collins for a home seller?

Fort Collins is a home rule city and the county seat of Larimer County, built along the Cache la Poudre River at the foot of the Front Range foothills, about 60 miles north of Denver. It is the fourth-largest city in Colorado, with 169,810 residents at the 2020 census and a 2024 estimate of 170,924.

A city this size has several kinds of housing, from older homes near the historic Old Town district to neighborhoods that spread south as the city grew in the late twentieth century. Sellers here range from long-time owners to landlords and heirs, and the right way to sell depends mostly on the condition of the house and how quickly you need to move.

How did Fort Collins begin?

Fort Collins began as a U.S. Army post. The fort was established in 1864 as the successor to Camp Collins, which a June 1864 flood destroyed, and the Army decommissioned it in 1867.

The town was platted in 1867, and the county seat moved from LaPorte to Fort Collins in 1868. Colorado Agricultural College was founded in 1870 and held its first classes in 1879.

Wikipedia gives two different incorporation dates, so we leave the year out here. The article also notes that the Northern Arapaho were centered on the Cache la Poudre Valley before the city existed.

Which school district covers Fort Collins?

Poudre School District runs the public K-12 schools in Fort Collins and nearby towns. It operates four comprehensive high schools, four alternative high schools, ten middle schools and 32 elementary schools, and it adds about 400 to 500 students each year.

Charter and private options exist as well. A buyer's school questions usually come down to the attendance zone for a single address, so have that answer ready or tell the buyer to ask the district.

How do people get around Fort Collins?

Interstate 25 runs north to south along the east side of the city, and US 287 becomes College Avenue, the busiest street in town.

  • MAX Bus Rapid Transit follows the Mason Corridor parallel to College Avenue, from downtown to a transit center south of Harmony Road. It opened in May 2014 and takes about 15 minutes end to end.
  • Transfort is the city bus system, with more than a dozen routes.
  • Northern Colorado Regional Airport is nearby, and Denver International Airport is about 70 miles south.

Homes near MAX stops and College Avenue draw a different set of buyers and renters than houses in the outer neighborhoods, and that is worth mentioning when you describe your property.

What happened in the 1997 Fort Collins flood?

In July 1997 a flash flood followed about 31 hours of rain totaling 10 to 14 inches. It killed five people, caused about $5 million in damage to city property and roughly $140 million in damage to Colorado State University, including flooding its library.

After an event like that, flood status is a fair question to expect. If your house lies near the Poudre or one of its drainage channels, a buyer or lender will want to know its flood zone status. A cash buyer will look at the same facts but will not need a lender's flood determination to close.

Does Fort Collins require landlords to register rentals?

Yes. Since January 1, 2025, most long-term rental properties, meaning homes rented for 30 days or more, must register annually with the city and certify that they meet minimum housing standards.

If you own a rental and plan to sell, this affects you in a few ways:

For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, Larimer County set February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half, and April 30 for payment in full. February 28 fell on a Saturday that year, and payments received the following Monday, March 2, were treated as timely.

Payments can be made online by credit or debit card or by electronic check, which has no fee. You can also mail a check to the Larimer County Treasurer, P.O. Box 2336, Fort Collins, CO 80522, or pay in person at 200 W. Oak St., Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The treasurer's phone is (970) 498-7020.

Late payments carry interest under Colorado law. If a mortgage escrow pays your taxes, ask your servicer for the payoff and escrow refund details. The county page does not describe proration at closing, so your title company is the right source for how the tax is split.

What does it cost to record a deed in Colorado?

Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed conveying real property, and any partial $100 counts as a full one. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and no fee applies if the consideration is $500 or less.

On a $400,000 sale, the fee comes to $400. Your purchase contract states which party pays it.

How does a direct cash sale of a Fort Collins house work?

A direct sale replaces the listing process with a short list of steps, and you can stop at any of them.

  • You describe the house, its condition and the date you would like to close.
  • The buyer reviews the details and may walk through the property.
  • You get an offer and decide whether to accept it.
  • A title company checks ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the closing papers.
  • You sign the deed, it is recorded with the Larimer County clerk and recorder, and you receive the proceeds.

Since the buyer pays with cash, no lender appraisal or loan approval sits in the middle of the timeline. We cannot quote a price or a closing date without seeing the property, and we do not promise either in advance.

Yes. You can sell a rental that is still occupied, and an investor buyer may keep the tenants. If the property was registered with the city under the 2025 rental program, make sure the registration is current before closing.

Do I need to repair my Fort Collins house before selling?

No. A cash sale is made as-is, so the buyer prices the repairs into the offer. You skip contractor bids, inspections ordered by a lender and showings.

When is the Larimer County property tax deadline?

For taxes payable in 2026, the first half was due February 28, the full payment option was due April 30, and the second half is due June 15. The county treasurer can confirm dates for the current year.

Is Fort Collins in a flood area?

Parts of it are near the Cache la Poudre River and drainage channels. A 1997 flash flood killed five people and caused heavy damage, so buyers often check a parcel's flood zone. Look up your address on the city's maps.

What is the Colorado deed fee on a home sale?

One cent per $100 of the price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when the deed is recorded. The sales contract decides who pays it.

Where is Arvada and how big is it?

Arvada is a home rule city about 7 miles northwest of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver, mostly in Jefferson County with a small part in Adams County. It covers about 39.6 square miles at an elevation near 5,500 feet, and its location puts it in the Front Range Urban Corridor.

The 2020 census counted 124,402 residents, which made Arvada the seventh largest city in Colorado, and a 2024 estimate put it at 121,873. Nearly all of them (121,510) live on the Jefferson County side, so most Arvada sellers deal with the Jefferson County Assessor and Treasurer.

The city is mostly residential, with some light industry and professional offices. Main commercial streets are Wadsworth Boulevard, Ralston Road and Kipling Street.

What is the history of Arvada?

Arvada began as a farming and gold rush area. Lewis Ralston documented gold near Ralston Creek in 1850, and the Colorado Central Railroad reached the area in 1870.

The townsite was platted on December 1, 1870, as Ralston Point and renamed Arvada, after Hiram Arvada Haskin, the brother-in-law of settler Mary Wadsworth. The town incorporated in 1904, became a statutory city in 1951 and a home rule municipality in 1963.

  • Pascal celery earned Arvada the nickname Celery Capital of the World in the early 1900s.
  • Colorado's first supermarket opened here in 1947.
  • The Rocky Flats Plant, which made nuclear weapon triggers, ran from 1952 to 1992 just outside the city, and the Rocky Flats National Wildlife Refuge is now nearby.

The city grew as a Denver suburb after World War II.

Which parts of Arvada do buyers and sellers talk about?

Olde Town Arvada is the historic core, with shops, restaurants and a transit hub. Around it sit older neighborhoods with smaller lots, while newer subdivisions spread toward the edges of the city.

ItemDetail
RailRTD G Line stations at Arvada Ridge, Olde Town Arvada and 60th and Sheridan/Arvada Gold Strike, running to Denver Union Station
AmtrakThe California Zephyr passes through Arvada daily
HighwaysInterstate 76 begins at its western end here, with I-25, I-270, US 36 and US 287 nearby
School districtsJefferson County School District R-1 and, for the Adams County part, Westminster Public Schools

Other draws in town include the Arvada Center for the Arts and Humanities, the Cussler Museum and the Two Ponds National Wildlife Refuge. Because so much of the housing stock came with the post war suburban growth, check the age of the roof, furnace and sewer line before you price.

What is Jefferson County, and why does it matter to an Arvada seller?

Jefferson County is the county that handles most Arvada paperwork. It was founded on November 1, 1861, covers 774 square miles along the Front Range next to Denver, and had 582,910 residents in 2020. Golden is the county seat, and Lakewood is the largest city.

The county includes Arvada (in part), Wheat Ridge, Westminster (in part), Edgewater, Morrison and Superior (in part), plus mountain communities such as Conifer and Pine. Its employers include Coors Brewing Company in Golden and the Colorado School of Mines, and the Denver Federal Center in Lakewood is described as the largest concentration of federal agencies outside Washington, D.C.

Because the county seat is in Golden, a trip to the Treasurer or the courthouse means leaving Arvada.

What is the weather like, and what does it mean for an Arvada house?

Arvada has a humid continental climate, with an average annual precipitation of about 16 inches and the wettest months in spring and summer. The mean annual high is about 65.7 degrees and the mean low about 37.1.

Front Range spring storms are the usual test for roofs, gutters and windows. Buyers who inspect an older Arvada house will look closely at roof age, drainage near the foundation and the furnace, and those are the items that sellers tend to price in or repair.

Ask your insurance agent what your policy says about hail and wind before you list, because an open claim can complicate a closing.

What are Arvada's short-term rental rules?

Arvada allows short-term rentals of less than 30 days with a city license. At a February 2025 council workshop, staff said the city had more than 800 short-term rentals and only about 250 to 300 were licensed, and that the annual registration fee was $150.

A house that was used as a short-term rental may carry unresolved licensing or complaint history, so buyers sometimes ask for proof. If you are selling an Arvada property that was rented to guests, gather the license, any city notices and tax filings first.

The same workshop explained why the city cares. Code enforcement staff said short-term rental complaints were about 3% of their cases, 23 out of more than 2,000, but that an unlicensed owner is hard to find, since many are LLCs. A council member also cited the city's housing needs assessment, which found Arvada short about 2,790 rental units. Council directed staff to find a third party vendor, estimated at $18,000, to bring unlicensed rentals into compliance.

How does property tax work for Arvada homeowners?

Jefferson County values the property, and the Jefferson County Treasurer collects the tax. The Treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2520, in Golden, and the phone is 303-271-8330.

  • Taxes above $25 are due in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by the last day of February and the second by June 15.
  • For 2026 the state guide lists residential assessment rates of 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.
  • Real property is revalued in odd numbered years, and valuation notices go out by May 1.
  • Protest deadline: June 8 under the standard state schedule.

A tax lien attaches to every county property with taxes owing on January 1 each year. If the owner has not paid by late October, the county sells the lien at its annual sale, and the owner then has three years to redeem it. The Treasurer's office is closed on Fridays.

What are your options for selling a house in Arvada?

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer for the house as is. Listing usually brings repairs, showings and weeks of waiting on a buyer's loan.

A cash sale suits sellers with an inherited house, a vacant rental, deferred repairs or a tight deadline. The deed is recorded with the county clerk, and any tax owing is paid from the proceeds. We can look at your Arvada address and explain the choices before you commit to anything.

What is the largest city in Jefferson County?

Lakewood is the largest city in Jefferson County, and the county seat is Golden.

Which county is Arvada in?

Most of Arvada lies in Jefferson County, and a small part (2,892 residents in 2020) is in Adams County. Your tax bill shows which county applies.

What is the Arvada property tax protest deadline?

Under the standard state schedule the protest deadline is June 8. Read your own Notice of Valuation, since counties can use an alternate schedule.

Can I sell my Arvada house with unpaid property tax?

Yes. Back taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing, and the title company gets the exact figure from the Jefferson County Treasurer.

Are short-term rentals allowed in Arvada?

Yes, with a license. The annual fee was reported at $150 in early 2025, and officials said many rentals were unlicensed.

What did Rocky Flats do near Arvada?

The Rocky Flats Plant operated from 1952 to 1992 as a manufacturing complex that produced nuclear weapon triggers. The site is now the Rocky Flats National Wildlife Refuge.

Which school districts serve Arvada?

Jefferson County School District R-1 serves the Jefferson County part, and Westminster Public Schools serves the Adams County part.

Where is Boulder and how did it start?

Boulder is a home rule city and the seat of Boulder County, at the base of the Rocky Mountain foothills about 25 miles northwest of Denver. The city covers about 27.4 square miles, and the 40th parallel runs along Baseline Road.

Prospectors led by Thomas Aikins reached Boulder Canyon in late 1858, and gold turned up along Boulder Creek in early 1859. The city incorporated on November 4, 1871. The University of Colorado was authorized in 1861 and opened in 1877.

The 2020 census counted 108,250 residents, and a 2024 estimate put the city at 106,803.

Who employs people in Boulder?

The university, research labs and a few large companies dominate. These are 2022 figures from the city's financial report as summarized on Wikipedia.

What is Boulder's weather like for homeowners?

Boulder is semi-arid with many sunny days, about 21 inches of precipitation a year and 88 inches of snow in an average season. Summers bring frequent afternoon thunderstorms and about 30 days at or above 90 degrees.

The record high is 104 degrees (June 25, 2012) and the record low is minus 33 (January 17, 1930). Heavy snow load and sudden storms are the reasons buyers check roofs and drainage on foothill houses.

Is flood risk a factor when selling a Boulder house?

Yes. The city calls itself the number one flash flood risk community in Colorado, and a house in a mapped floodplain changes the insurance conversation.

  • With most policies there is a 30-day wait before flood insurance takes effect, so buyers should not wait.
  • The city joined the federal Community Rating System in 1992 and earned a Class 5 rating in early 2013, giving standard policyholders a 25% discount.
  • An elevation certificate prepared by a Colorado licensed surveyor can lower premiums, and the city lets you search for one on file.
  • New residential construction must sit at least two feet above the 100-year flood elevation.

Check the city's interactive floodplain map for your address before you list.

What did the 2013 flood do to Boulder?

Rain began around September 9, 2013, and the flooding grew worst on September 11 and 12. Several locations in the city of Boulder recorded 15 to 20 inches between September 9 and 15, which beat Boulder County's yearly average of about 20.7 inches in just five days.

Boulder Creek peaked above 5,000 cubic feet per second on September 12, against a normal 150 to 200. In Boulder County, 262 homes were destroyed and nearly 300 more were damaged, and three deaths were confirmed. A major disaster was declared for the county.

That event is the reason floodplain questions come up early in a Boulder sale. Buyers and lenders know the history.

What did the Marshall Fire change in Boulder County?

The Marshall Fire burned in Boulder County from December 30, 2021, to January 1, 2022. Superior was evacuated first and Louisville was ordered out later.

An estimated 1,084 structures burned and 149 more were damaged across 6,026 acres, with gusts up to 115 mph. The sheriff's office announced in June 2023 that the cause involved two separate occurrences, embers on the Twelve Tribes property and a sparking Xcel Energy power line.

The fire was in Superior and Louisville, not the city of Boulder, but it is part of the county's recent history for any homeowner here.

What rental rules affect a Boulder sale?

A rental property in Boulder needs an approved rental license before it can be used or advertised as a rental. Approval depends on inspections for health and safety, mechanical systems and energy efficiency.

The efficiency piece is SmartRegs, which requires all licensed rental housing in the city to meet a basic energy standard. The city says the approval process can take several weeks at a minimum. If a buyer plans to rent the house, they have to start this process, and the SmartRegs guide is aimed at realtors in that situation too.

Owners can reach compliance through a prescriptive pathway or a performance pathway, and the city lists licensed inspection companies. Contractors are told to write invoices that describe the work done, because a SmartRegs inspector uses it to update the property score. Tenants can even earn the landlord a point by taking the SmartRegs tenant quiz.

How do roads, transit and open space work in Boulder?

Boulder has RTD bus service, including the Flatiron Flyer bus rapid transit route to Denver, and US 36 and state highways. The city has no rail transit, and it has an extensive network of bike paths and underpasses.

Boulder Valley School District runs most public schools, with a few northeast areas served by St. Vrain Valley. Nearly 60% of city open space, about 35,584 acres, is open to the public, and the Open Space and Mountain Parks department manages about 8,000 acres of forest land west of the city.

How are Boulder property taxes and the deed handled?

Boulder County bills the tax, and the state schedule applies: pay in full by April 30 or in two halves by the last day of February and June 15. For 2026 the state guide lists residential rates of 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.

The Boulder County Clerk and Recorder records the deed. The recording fee for a document was $43 effective July 1, 2025, and a transfer deed over $500 is assessed the state documentary fee of $.01 per $100. In person service is Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and there are drop boxes in Boulder, Lafayette and Longmont.

The county uses the grantee's mailing address on the deed to send the tax statements after a sale. Recorder documents also need a top margin of at least one inch, and the recorder may refuse a document that does not meet the margin rules, so have the title company handle the format.

What are your options for selling a house in Boulder?

You can list it, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. Boulder houses with flood exposure, unlicensed rental history or deferred maintenance often take longer on the open market.

A cash sale is as is, so there are no repairs to arrange. Send us your Boulder address and we will explain how a sale would work.

Boulder Creek peaked above 5,000 cubic feet per second on September 12, 2013, and 262 homes were destroyed in Boulder County.

How far is Boulder from Denver?

About 25 miles northwest of Denver, at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains.

Parts of it are. Use the city's interactive floodplain map, and note that flood insurance has a 30-day waiting period.

Do I need a rental license to rent my Boulder house?

Yes. The city requires an approved rental license before a property can be used or advertised as a rental, and licensing includes SmartRegs energy standards.

What is the Boulder County recording fee?

The county lists $43 per document as of July 1, 2025, plus a state documentary fee of $.01 per $100 on transfer deeds over $500.

Where is Commerce City and what is it known for?

Commerce City is a home rule city in Adams County, just north of Denver, at an elevation of 5,191 feet. It covers about 36 square miles and is part of the Front Range Urban Corridor.

The city has grown fast. The 2020 census counted 62,418 residents, up 35.9% from 2010, and the Census Bureau estimated 72,345 for July 1, 2025. That is a 15.9% rise from the 2020 base, the largest gain among the four Colorado cities in the Census comparison we used.

Owner-occupancy here is high, which means most Commerce City sellers are homeowners and not landlords.

How did Commerce City get its name and shape?

The area dates to 1859, when John D. Henderson set up a ranch, trading post and hotel on Henderson Island to serve gold seekers. The first area school opened in 1871 as a one-room schoolhouse.

A refinery was established in 1930, and the Rocky Mountain Arsenal was founded in 1942. Residents voted 251 to 24 in July 1952 to incorporate as Commerce Town. In 1962 the town annexed part of Derby, gained city status and took the name Commerce City. In 2007 voters chose by more than two to one to keep that name.

Henderson Island is now the site of the Adams County Regional Park and Fairgrounds. Rose Hill and southern Adams City were part of the original 1952 town.

What drives the Commerce City economy?

Heavy industry and logistics anchor Commerce City. The Suncor Energy refinery has a capacity of 98,000 barrels per day and is described as the largest refinery in the Rocky Mountain region.

Census data supports the logistics picture. Transportation and warehousing receipts in 2022 were about $1.46 billion, far above the $91 million in health care and social assistance receipts. The city's northern community extends north of Denver International Airport.

  • Dick's Sporting Goods Park is a soccer stadium and home of the Colorado Rapids.
  • The Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge covers 27 square miles, and its only entrance is in Commerce City.
  • City parks and open space total 840 acres, with 25 miles of trails.

A house near the refinery or industrial corridors can be harder to sell to buyers who dislike the proximity, which is one reason an as-is buyer who does not care about the setting is an option.

Which school districts serve Commerce City?

Adams County School District 27J and Adams 14 each include parts of the city. Adams City High School is the comprehensive high school of Adams 14, and a new building opened at 72nd and Quebec in 2009.

The split matters when you sell, because buyers with children usually ask which district a house is in. Check the district boundary for your address before you advertise. The Census figure for people under 18 is 28.7%, the highest of the four cities we compared.

When are Adams County property taxes due?

Adams County bills Commerce City property, and its Treasurer lists three ways to pay. You may split the bill into two payments due February 28 and June 15, or pay all of it by April 30.

The county does not accept partial payments, and taxes of $25 or less do not qualify for the half-payment option. Payments with a U.S. postmark on or before the date are treated as on time. After that, delinquent interest is added, and the county says taxes must be paid by 5:00 PM on October 31 to avoid fees tied to the tax lien sale.

Colorado law, in section 39-10-104.5, sets the same February, April and June dates and adds interest of 1% per month on late amounts. The Justia copy we read was the 2022 version, so confirm the current wording on the county's Adams County due dates page.

When a Commerce City house sells, the title company prorates the current year's tax. Make sure earlier years are paid, because a lien on the parcel has to be cleared before the deed transfers.

Does Commerce City allow short-term rentals?

Yes. As of January 1, 2025, short-term rentals are legal in Commerce City, subject to zoning and licensing. The city defines one as a stay of fewer than 30 days in a duplex or detached house.

  • The license costs $150 and is valid for a year from issue, with annual renewal.
  • A responsible agent must be reachable 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and live within 30 miles.
  • Applications go through the city's eTRAKiT system and are processed in the order received.
  • HOA rules, parking and guest limits are listed in Ordinances 2648 and 2653.

If you inherited or bought a house that someone ran as a nightly rental before 2025, check that the license history is clean before you sell.

What do households and weather look like in Commerce City?

Commerce City households are larger than in the other cities we compared, at 2.95 people per household in the 2020 to 2024 Census data. Median gross rent was $1,880, the highest of the four, and 88.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Wikipedia lists a mean daily maximum of 65.3 degrees for the year, peaking near 88 degrees in July, and winter minimums of 21 to 22 degrees. A house here sees hot summer afternoons and freezing nights, so check the furnace, the air conditioner and any exposed plumbing before an inspection.

The Census Bureau also reports that 30.5% of residents over age 5 speak a language other than English at home and 25.8% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. If you list, clear disclosures in plain language help every kind of buyer, and if you sell for cash the paperwork is shorter.

What are your options for selling a Commerce City house?

You can list the house, sell it yourself or accept an as-is cash purchase. With 77.2% of homes owner-occupied and a median value near $500,000, most local sellers have equity to protect, so compare net proceeds rather than only the headline price.

A listing brings showings and inspection requests. A cash sale skips those, and the closing date can follow your schedule. We buy houses in Commerce City in any condition and the offer carries no obligation. Our team can answer questions about what to expect at the title company.

One cost every seller sees: Colorado's documentary fee on a deed is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500, so a $500,000 sale carries $50. County recording pages describe the fee this way, and it appears on the settlement statement along with prorated taxes.

How many people live in Commerce City?

The Census Bureau estimated 72,345 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census count was 62,418.

What are the Adams County property tax deadlines?

The county lists February 28 and June 15 for two payments, or April 30 for a single full payment. Partial payments are not accepted.

What is the median home value in Commerce City?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes is $499,700. Your house may differ, so treat that figure as a benchmark.

Do I need a license to rent my Commerce City house short term?

Yes. The city requires a $150 license, renewed each year, and a responsible agent within 30 miles who can respond around the clock.

Is Commerce City mostly owner-occupied?

Yes. The Census Bureau reports a 77.2% owner-occupied housing rate for 2020 to 2024, the highest of the four Colorado cities we compared, with 22,415 households in the city.

Which school district is my Commerce City house in?

It depends on the address. Both Adams County School District 27J and Adams 14 include parts of the city, so check the district's boundary lookup.

Where is Grand Junction, and how big is it?

Grand Junction is a home rule city and the county seat of Mesa County, 247 miles west-southwest of Denver, and the largest city in Colorado outside the Front Range Urban Corridor. It is the economic and cultural center of the Western Slope.

The 2020 census counted 65,560 residents, which made it the 17th most populous municipality in the state, and the 2025 estimate shown on Wikipedia is 71,780. The city covers about 40 square miles at an elevation of 4,646 feet.

Grand Junction facts in one table

The source article also gives a metro population of over 162,000 for 2025, which is a wider area than the city itself.

How did Grand Junction get its name and start?

The name refers to the junction of the Colorado River, once called the Grand River, with the Gunnison River. Before incorporation, the community was known as Ute.

The Ute people lived in the region before European-American farmers arrived in the 1880s. In September 1881 the former Ute Indian Territory was abolished and the Utes were moved to a reservation. George Addison Crawford incorporated the town on July 22, 1882. Railroads reached the city in 1882 from Pueblo by narrow gauge and in 1890 by standard gauge from New Castle.

Fruit growing became important by the late nineteenth century, especially between Grand Junction and Palisade, with peaches, pears, apricots, plums, cherries and grapes. Wineries opened in the area beginning in the late twentieth century.

What does the high desert climate mean for a house?

Grand Junction has a cold semi-arid climate with hot summers and about 9 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs and exteriors face sun and heat more than rain.

  • July averages 78.2 degrees F, and January averages 27.4 degrees F.
  • About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 degrees or higher.
  • The average last freeze is April 25 and the average first freeze is October 11.

Long stretches of heat are hard on air conditioners, roofing and exterior paint. A buyer's inspector will often check the cooling system and the roof, and a cash buyer prices what they find instead of asking you to repair it.

What drives Grand Junction's economy?

Health care, tourism, agriculture, livestock and energy are the main contributors, according to Wikipedia. The largest employers it lists give a sense of the job base.

EmployerEmployees
Mesa County Valley School District 513,465
St. Mary's Regional Hospital2,846
Colorado Mesa University1,173

Energy has a history of boom and bust here. Oil shale development lifted the area in the 1970s and early 1980s, and Exxon's withdrawal in 1982, known locally as Black Sunday, caused an economic bust.

Which schools and college are in Grand Junction?

Mesa County Valley School District 51 provides public K-12 education in the area. Wikipedia names Fruita Monument, Grand Junction, Central and Palisade high schools among its five, plus an R-5 High School.

Colorado Mesa University enrolls nearly 10,000 students and is the largest university in western Colorado. Owners of rentals near campus are one group that sometimes decides to sell.

What roads, rail and flights serve Grand Junction?

Interstate 70 links Grand Junction east to Glenwood Springs and Denver and west toward Green River, Utah. U.S. Highways 6 and 50 also meet in the city, and State Highway 340 runs through the Redlands to Fruita.

  • Grand Junction Regional Airport is the largest airport in western Colorado and the third largest in the state.
  • Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at Grand Junction Station.
  • Grand Valley Transit provides local buses, and Bustang offers intercity service.

The city sits in the Grand Valley, a river valley about 30 miles long. Nearby areas include the Redlands, Palisade, Fruita and Loma, and a buyer may compare a house in the city with homes in those communities.

Are short-term rentals regulated in Grand Junction?

Yes. Any property owner who plans to run a short-term rental inside city limits must get a license from the City of Grand Junction and renew it every year, under Ordinance No. 5163 adopted July 5, 2023.

The application fee is $275 per property. The city also caps how many residentially zoned lots can hold a primary short-term rental.

  • Downtown (North Ave to I-70B, Highway 50 to N 17th St): no more than 7 percent of residentially zoned lots.
  • Outside downtown: no more than 3 percent.
  • Lots with four or fewer units: one primary and one secondary rental allowed.
  • Lots with five or more units: no more than 10 percent of units.

If you own a house that has been run as a short-term rental, check whether the license is current before talking to a buyer, because the cap affects who can get a new license. Community Development is at 250 N 5th Street and can be reached at 970-244-1430. The city page does not say whether a license transfers on sale, so ask the office.

When are Mesa County property taxes due?

Mesa County's assessor lists the key dates: the Treasurer mails tax bills on January 31, the first installment is due February 28, full payment is due April 30 and the second installment is due June 15.

If you sell between January and the payment dates, the tax for the prior year may still be unpaid, so the title company will want to see the balance.

What does the state charge to record a deed?

Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed conveying real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and nothing is owed at $500 or less.

On a $300,000 sale that comes to $300. The contract usually names the party who pays it.

How does a cash sale work in Grand Junction?

You contact us with the address and condition, we review it, and you get an offer you can accept or decline. A title company confirms ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the deed, and the deed is recorded in Mesa County.

There is no lender in the middle, so closing depends on title work and the date you choose. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

What county is Grand Junction in?

Mesa County. Grand Junction is the county seat and the largest city in the county, so property taxes are billed by the Mesa County Treasurer and deeds are recorded in Mesa County.

When is the second property tax payment due in Mesa County?

June 15. The first installment is due February 28, and paying in full is due April 30, according to the Mesa County assessor's key dates page.

Do I need a license to rent my Grand Junction house short term?

Yes. The city requires an annual short-term rental license with a $275 application fee per property, and it limits the share of residential lots that can have a primary short-term rental.

Can I sell my Grand Junction house without repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, cooling system or cosmetic items first. The offer reflects the condition.

How hot does Grand Junction get?

About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees F or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 or higher. That heat is why inspectors look closely at cooling systems and roofs.

How did Erie start, and does the coal history still affect houses?

Erie began as a coal town. Coal turned up in the mid-1860s in the southwest corner of Weld County, and the town took its name from Erie, Pennsylvania, the old home of early settler Richard Van Valkenburg.

Railroads arrived in 1870 and 1871 and carried coal toward Denver and nearby communities. The first official underground mine opened in 1876 under Ira Austin. Unlike a temporary mining camp, miners here owned homes in town.

Most local mines had closed by 1960, and the Eagle Mine shut in 1978. For a seller, the practical point is that older homes near the original town center may carry old additions, older plumbing and electrical systems, and records that take more digging to assemble. A buyer who purchases as-is does not need all of that fixed before closing.

Floods are also part of the record. Major floods hit in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built around Coal Creek after the 1972 flood. If your lot is near the creek, expect a buyer or lender to ask about flood zone status.

How fast has Erie grown, and what does that mean for sellers?

Erie grew 65.6 percent between the 2010 and 2020 censuses, from roughly 18,100 residents to 30,038, and the 2024 estimate is 38,594. That pace suggests that a large share of local homes are fairly new compared with other Colorado towns.

For a seller, newer construction can mean fewer deferred repairs but also more neighbors offering similar homes. Some common situations we hear about in fast-growing suburbs include:

  • Homeowners who need to relocate for work before a listing could reasonably wrap up.
  • Owners of an inherited house who live out of state.
  • Landlords tired of managing a rental from a distance.
  • Sellers carrying a mortgage on a house that needs a new roof, flooring or paint.

None of these need a retail listing to be solved. A direct sale to a cash buyer skips showings, staging and buyer financing contingencies, which is the main reason people in these situations ask about it.

What roads, transit and airports serve Erie?

Interstate 25 runs along Erie's eastern border at Exit 232, and from there it is about 22 miles south to downtown Denver and 41 miles north to Fort Collins.

  • E-470 lies to the south.
  • State Highway 7 and State Highway 52 cross the area.
  • US 287 forms the western boundary.
  • Erie Municipal Airport (EIK) is town-owned, about three miles west of I-25 on Highway 7, with a 4,700-foot concrete runway.

Access to I-25 and E-470 is one reason commuters buy here, and it is a point worth stating in any sale conversation. Buyers who drive to Denver, Boulder or the north Front Range tend to ask about commute times first.

Which schools serve Erie homes?

Erie High School is the only high school in the town and belongs to the St. Vrain Valley School District. It opened in 2005 and was expanded in 2018, and it enrolled 1,727 students in the 2024-2025 school year.

Wikipedia notes that the school has paused open enrollment because of overcapacity, so students outside its attendance zone are not admitted. That makes the school zone worth confirming before any buyer assumes access. Parents often ask which school a specific address feeds, and the district can answer by address.

We have not confirmed the district boundaries for every Erie neighborhood, so check with the district if a zone matters to your sale.

What is Erie's weather, and how does it affect a house?

Erie has a dry Front Range climate with average annual precipitation of 16.17 inches. May is the wettest month at 2.60 inches and January is the driest at 0.57 inches.

Dry air does not mean low risk to the structure. Roofs, gutters, decks and exterior paint take sun and wind year-round, and an older roof is one of the first items a buyer's inspector flags. A cash buyer prices a worn roof into the offer and does not ask you to replace it first.

When are property taxes due in Weld County, and what happens at closing?

On the Weld County side, taxes are due January 1 for the previous year and can be paid in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by February 28 and the second by June 15. Weld's treasurer states that partial payments are not accepted and that postmarks on or before the due date count.

Late interest rises by month. For example, the first half picks up 1 percent in March and 6 percent by August. Weld offers payment online at weldtax.com, by mail to PO Box 458, Greeley, or in person at 1400 N 17th Avenue, Greeley.

If your parcel is on the Boulder County side, the Boulder County Treasurer collects the tax, so confirm the figures with that office. The title company usually orders a certificate of taxes due and handles the proration at closing. Weld lists a Certificate of Taxes Due request form on its treasurer pages.

What does Colorado charge to record a deed?

Colorado charges a documentary fee of one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed recorded for real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. The fee is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and the statute sets no fee at or below $500.

On a $500,000 sale, one cent per $100 works out to $500. Who pays it is usually settled in the purchase contract, so read that line before you sign.

How does a cash sale of an Erie house work?

A cash sale follows a short sequence of steps, and you decide at each stage whether to go on.

  • You share the address, condition and your timing.
  • The buyer reviews the property and may visit it.
  • You receive an offer, and you can accept, counter or decline.
  • A title company runs the title search, orders tax figures and prepares the deed.
  • You sign, the deed is recorded with the county clerk where the parcel sits, and you are paid.

Because no lender is involved, there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on. The pace is set mostly by title work and your preferred closing date. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

Which county is Erie, Colorado in?

Both. Erie lies mostly in southwest Weld County (about 58 percent of residents) and partly in eastern Boulder County (about 42 percent). Your tax bill shows which county covers your parcel.

Can I sell my Erie house as-is?

Yes. Homeowners can sell in current condition to a cash buyer without repairs, cleaning or staging. The offer reflects what the house needs, so a worn roof or dated kitchen lowers the number but does not block the sale.

Who pays property tax when an Erie house sells?

The title company usually prorates it between seller and buyer at closing based on a certificate of taxes due. Colorado bills taxes in arrears, so the seller typically owes a share for the months owned. Ask your title officer for the exact split.

How much is the state deed fee in Colorado?

The documentary fee is one cent per $100 of the sale price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when a deed is recorded. The contract decides which side pays it.

Does being near Coal Creek affect my sale?

It can. Erie had major floods in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built along Coal Creek afterward. Buyers and lenders may check flood zone status for homes near the creek, so find out your parcel's status before you list or sell.

Where is Englewood, Colorado, and how big is it?

Englewood is a small city in western Arapahoe County, immediately south of Denver in the South Platte River valley. It covers about 6.6 square miles at an elevation of 5,348 feet.

The 2020 census counted 33,659 residents, up from 30,255 in 2010, and the Census Bureau estimated 35,305 for July 1, 2025. Density was 5,127 people per square mile in 2020, the highest of the four Colorado cities in the Census table we used.

Households here are small, and just under half of homes are owner-occupied, so Englewood sellers include many owners of small houses and condos as well as landlords.

What is Englewood's history?

Gold was found near the mouth of what became Little Dry Creek in 1858, and Thomas Skerritt built a home called Orchard Place in 1860. The town was incorporated on May 9, 1903, with J.C. Jones as its first mayor.

In 1948 the city bought 2,500 acres on the Platte Canyon, which led to McLellan Reservoir. City Park was sold in 1965 to make way for the Cinderella City mall, which opened in 1968. About 30 years later the city demolished the defunct mall and replaced it with a transit-oriented development around the light-rail stop.

What are the main areas of Englewood?

Englewood is divided by Broadway and Hampden Avenue into four quadrants, and each has a different housing mix.

  • Northwest: the oldest section, with downtown, City Center and housing from the 1910s. A former General Iron site is awaiting redevelopment.
  • Southwest: newer housing along with many industrial facilities, plus Belleview Park.
  • Southeast: almost entirely residential and newer than the north and southwest, reaching the Highline Canal.
  • Northeast: the hospital complex that includes Swedish Medical Center and Craig Hospital.

Hampden Hills is described as the newest and wealthiest part of the city, with many apartment complexes. Housing age varies a lot from quadrant to quadrant, and buyers and their inspectors will ask how old the systems in a house are.

Who are the largest employers in Englewood?

Hospitals are the backbone of the Englewood economy. The 2023 top employer list on Wikipedia is led by Swedish Medical Center and Craig Hospital, followed by Groove Toyota, Metro Community Provider Network, Veolia Transportation, Rollinc Staffing, Walmart, Meadow Gold Dairies, Ouray Sportswear and American Bottling.

The Census Bureau's 2022 figures show health care and social assistance receipts of about $1.13 billion, and retail sales per capita of $46,983, the highest of the four cities compared. That per-capita figure is well above Denver's $20,973, and 75.1% of those aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force.

For a seller, hospital and retail jobs mean steady local rental demand, but they do not help a house that needs a new roof or sewer line.

Who lives in Englewood, and what does that mean for sellers?

Englewood is an older, well-educated city with small households. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates give a picture of who might buy or rent a house here.

  • People aged 65 and over make up 15.0% of residents, and 14.5% are under 18.
  • 49.3% of adults aged 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Median household income is $86,800, and 7.7% of residents are in poverty.
  • 80.7% of people lived in the same house a year earlier.
  • 1,245 residents are veterans.

An older population often means estates and downsizing. Heirs who live out of state and inherit an Englewood house sometimes want a clean sale without managing repairs from a distance.

How do schools, transit and weather affect an Englewood house?

Englewood Public Schools serves most of the city, with small portions in Littleton Public Schools and Sheridan Public Schools. Part of Cherry Hills Village is also in the Englewood district.

The Englewood station on RTD's D Line sits in the Civic Center, and the line runs from Littleton to 18th and California in Denver. Mean travel time to work was 22.6 minutes in the 2020 to 2024 Census data.

The climate is cold semi-arid, drier than much of the Front Range at 10.42 inches of annual precipitation, with record readings of 108 degrees and minus 33. Wide temperature swings are tough on roofs and exterior finishes.

What are Arapahoe County's property tax dates for Englewood owners?

Arapahoe County bills Englewood property tax under the same state calendar as the rest of Colorado. Colorado statute 39-10-104.5 lets an owner pay in two halves, due on or before the last day of February and by June 15, or pay in one payment on or before the last day of April.

Interest on late amounts runs at 1% per month, and any part of a month counts as a whole month. Installments under $25 cannot be split and must be paid in full by April 30. The Justia copy we opened is the 2022 version, so confirm the current rule with the Arapahoe County Treasurer.

When an Englewood house sells, the title company prorates the current year's tax through the closing date. Unpaid taxes from earlier years must be cleared before the deed can transfer cleanly.

What are Englewood's short-term rental rules?

Englewood requires every short-term rental operator to hold both a city sales and use tax license and a short-term rental license. In residential zones the operator must be the primary resident and live at the property at least 185 days a year.

  • Applications need a current deed on file with Arapahoe County, a notarized residency affidavit and two proofs of primary residence in residential zones.
  • Insurance must include at least $1 million in personal liability coverage.
  • Parking must include one permanent space per rented bedroom, with no more than two on the street.
  • Fee amounts on the city page rose January 1, 2026: $600 for a new application and $400 for a renewal, plus $75 for inspection and $200 at issuance.

A house that cannot meet these conditions may be worth less to a buyer who planned to rent it nightly, so check the license status before pricing.

How do you sell an Englewood house fast?

You can list with an agent, sell on your own or take a cash purchase. A listing may bring the highest price on a house in good shape, while a cash sale is the faster path for a house that needs work, has tenants or sits in an estate.

Colorado's documentary fee on a deed is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500. We buy houses in Englewood and nearby Arapahoe County in any condition. Tell us about the property, and you will get an answer with no obligation if you say no.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes in Englewood is $572,900. Treat it as a benchmark, since each house differs.

Which county is Englewood in?

Englewood is in Arapahoe County, where its deeds are recorded and its property taxes are billed.

Yes. You need a city sales and use tax license and a short-term rental license, and in residential zones you must live at the property at least 185 days a year.

State law allows two halves, due by the last day of February and by June 15, or a single payment by the last day of April.

Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so unfinished work does not have to be completed before closing.

What is the history of Fountain?

Fountain was founded in 1859 as a railroad shipping center for ranches and farms in the area. Wikipedia lists April 23, 1903 as the incorporation date in its infobox but says 1900 in the text, so we do not give a firm year.

One event from the early years still gets retold. On May 14, 1888, a freight train carrying about 18 tons of explosives collided with a passenger train in the city. Three people died, and the blast left a crater roughly 40 feet wide and 15 feet deep.

More recently, The New York Times called Fountain "America's Millennium City" in 1999, and the city won an All-America City award in 2002.

Which school districts serve Fountain?

The city runs its own utility. City of Fountain Utilities was established in 1919 and provides water and electric service to roughly 48,000 people in and around Fountain.

Its office is at 101 N Main St, and the phone number is (719) 322-2010. When a house sells, the seller schedules a final reading and the buyer opens a new account, so call the utility early, especially if you have a past-due balance.

Wikipedia also records a long-running PFAS contamination problem linked to a nearby Air Force base, and notes that the city said in 2020 that its water was safe to drink. Because the topic worries some buyers, have the city's water quality information on hand if it comes up.

How do you get around Fountain?

Fountain is served by a municipal bus that links the city to Pikes Peak State College, and by Bustang's Outrider line connecting Lamar, Pueblo and Colorado Springs.

  • Gather any prior-owner paperwork, permits and repair receipts you have.
  • Decide who will pay the Colorado deed fee, and write that into the contract.

The utility's own page also lists tools for customers, including an outage map, bill assistance, utility easement information and a note about calling 811 before digging. If your yard has an easement, tell the buyer, because it can limit fences and additions.

For a sale, the treasurer issues a Certificate of Taxes Due to verify the tax status of a property. Unpaid prior-year balances can be sold at the county's tax lien sale, so check for liens before closing. You can call (719) 520-7900 for a payoff figure.

The treasurer's main page links to an Important Dates page for the current deadlines, and we did not confirm those dates, so check it directly. Colorado's standard pattern, shown on Mesa County's assessor page, is full payment by April 30 or two halves due the end of February and June 15.
